## Summary

I am on **ChatGPT Pro** and use Codex CLI programmatically through `codex exec` from a Python application.

On **2026-10-01**, I observed what appears to be a billing / usage-metering error: **my included weekly Pro allowance and my separately purchased credit balance were both being consumed during the same period**.

Recorded values:

| Metric | Earlier | Later |
|---|---:|---:|
| Weekly included allowance remaining | **19%** | **2%** |
| Purchased credit balance | **~62,500** | **59,845** |
| Purchased credits deducted |  | **~2,655** |

I stopped all Codex activity after confirming this behavior in order to prevent further unexpected credit consumption.

The Usage dashboard attributes the purchased-credit deductions to **Service: Exec**, which matches my use of `codex exec`.

## Environment

- Subscription: **ChatGPT Pro**
- Codex CLI: **v0.159.2**
- Model: **GPT-5.6-Terra**
- Reasoning effort: **xhigh**
- Invocation: `codex exec`, launched programmatically from a Python application
- Billing context: ChatGPT Pro account with separately purchased ChatGPT/Codex usage credits
- Date observed: **2026-10-01**

## Evidence

I recorded two states:

### Earlier state
- Weekly included allowance: **19% remaining**
- Purchased credits: approximately **62,500**
- Usage dashboard already showed purchased-credit deductions under **Service: Exec**

### Later state
CLI `/status` reported:
- Account: **Pro**
- Codex: **v0.159.2**
- Model: **GPT-5.6-Terra (reasoning xhigh)**
- **Weekly limit: 2% left**
- **Credits: 59,845**

During this same interval, the included weekly allowance fell by 17 percentage points while approximately **2,655 purchased credits were also deducted**.

The issue is **not** that `xhigh` or a large workload consumes quota quickly. The issue is that **two separate usage pools were decreasing simultaneously**.

I have screenshots of:
1. the Usage dashboard showing multiple **Exec** credit deductions while weekly allowance remained; and
2. the CLI `/status` state showing **2% weekly allowance still remaining** and **59,845 credits**.

I have omitted account identifiers and session identifiers from this public report. I can provide timestamps/session details privately if maintainers need them for server-side reconciliation.

## Why this appears inconsistent with documented behavior

OpenAI's current Help Center documentation says:

> “Your plan's included usage is used first. After you hit plan limits, usage draws from your credit balance.”

Source:
https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12642688-using-credits-for-flexible-usage-in-chatgpt-personal-plans

The same page describes credits as a pay-as-you-go add-on for usage **beyond plan limits**, and says that already-used credits can be reviewed for a **verified billing correction**.

The current Codex pricing / usage documentation is here:
https://developers.openai.com/codex/pricing

Based on this, I expected purchased credits not to be charged while applicable included Pro usage was still available.

If there is another applicable limit bucket that can trigger paid-credit billing before the displayed weekly allowance reaches zero, please identify that bucket and explain why the weekly allowance continued to decrease at the same time.

## Actual behavior

While continuing the same `codex exec` workload:

1. Weekly included allowance was still available at **19% remaining**.
2. Purchased-credit transactions appeared under **Exec**.
3. The weekly allowance continued decreasing.
4. Purchased credits also continued decreasing.
5. Later `/status` showed **2% weekly allowance still remaining** and **59,845 credits**.
6. I stopped the workload to avoid further deductions.

So approximately **2,655 purchased credits were consumed before the displayed weekly allowance reached zero**.

## Expected behavior

One of the following would be expected:

- applicable included Pro usage continues to be consumed until the relevant plan limit is reached, and only then purchased credits begin to be used; or
- if a different limit bucket is actually responsible for switching to credits, that limit should be clearly exposed in `/status` / Usage and the billing transition should be auditable.

What should not happen without a clear explanation is for the displayed weekly included allowance and purchased credit balance to both decrease during the same usage period.

## Related reports

This appears closely related to several existing reports:

- **#49528 — Weekly allowance shows 25% remaining while Work/Codex credits decrease and credit usage history is empty**  
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49528

- **#41628 — Paid credits silently drawn down while 84% of weekly allowance remains**  
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41628

- **#15959 — Codex CLI consumed top-up credits while weekly quota was still available**  
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15959

- **#41220 — Abnormal Codex usage/quota depletion and usage-accounting inconsistencies — cross-report tracker**  
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41220

- **#28382 — Add a toggle to prevent automatic use of purchased Codex credits**  
  https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/28382

I am not claiming that all of these reports have the same root cause, but the user-visible billing symptom is very similar.

## Requested investigation and credit restoration

Please investigate the **server-side billing / metering ledger** for the affected `Exec` sessions and determine why purchased credits were selected while included weekly usage was still available and simultaneously decreasing.

I am specifically requesting:

1. **Restore the approximately 2,655 purchased credits** deducted during the period in which the weekly allowance decreased from 19% remaining to 2% remaining, if those deductions were made while applicable included Pro usage was still available.
2. Review the **entire affected period** and restore any additional purchased credits that were incorrectly deducted before the applicable included allowance was exhausted.
3. Confirm whether this account was affected by the same or a related issue as **#49528 / #41628 / #15959**.
4. Explain which exact limit is supposed to trigger purchased-credit billing for Pro, and why both balances decreased in parallel.
5. Improve `/status` / Usage so that any limit responsible for switching to paid credits is clearly visible and auditable.
6. Provide a way to disable automatic purchased-credit consumption, or require explicit confirmation before switching from included usage to paid credits.

I have also contacted OpenAI Support and requested a **billing correction / credit restoration**. A technical determination here would help reconcile the account and prevent additional unexpected charges.

Thanks.

1. Open the signed-in publisher dashboard at `https://chrome.google.com/u/2/webstore/devconsole/<publisher-id>` and an existing item's Store Listing page under that dashboard.
2. Explicitly authorize Codex to use the connected Chrome integration on those pages.
3. Ask Codex to read/edit the draft, with final submission/publication prohibited.
4. The open-tab inventory returns the correct URLs and titles, but claiming either tab fails before any form interaction.
5. Creating a new Chrome tab at the same exact dashboard URL returned `Not allowed`.

Changing the shell/filesystem/network permission profile to full access did not alter the existing-tab failure. No native desktop takeover or security-disabling workaround was used.

## Observed tool calls

- `browser.user.openTabs()` successfully returned the dashboard tabs.
- `browser.user.claimTab(<dashboard-tab-id>)` returned the gallery error.
- `cua.createBrowserTab("chrome", <exact-dashboard-url>, ...)` returned `Not allowed`.

Please document this limitation accurately and provide a supported way to prepare Developer Dashboard drafts without disabling Chrome Web Store protections. If resolving the hostname-level restriction requires Chromium changes, please identify the appropriate upstream route rather than presenting it as missing user authorization or a file-upload problem.

## Relevant source evidence

Chromium's `ChromeExtensionsClient::IsScriptableURL` returns `kCannotScriptGallery` when `IsWebstoreDomain(url)` matches:
https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/chrome/common/extensions/chrome_extensions_client.cc

The published hostname-level implementation of `IsWebstoreDomain` includes the host from `https://chrome.google.com/webstore`, irrespective of the specific page path:
https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/tags/135.0.7049.120/extensions/common/extension_urls.cc

This is evidence for a likely browser-level restriction; the installed Chrome build's internal call stack was not captured, and this report does not claim every control backend behaves identically.

## Summary
In a Codex desktop chat on Windows, every attempted local command fails before process creation. This blocks reading workspace instructions, inspecting Git state, making changes, and running tests. Retrying in a subsequent user turn produces the same failure.

## Environment
- Codex desktop on Windows
- Shell: PowerShell
- Local repository workspace
- Sandbox mode: workspace-write; managed restricted filesystem profile
- Codex version/build: unavailable in this session

## Reproduction
1. Open a local repository chat in Codex desktop.
2. Ask the agent to inspect or modify the repository.
3. Invoke exec_command with `Get-Location` and `login: false`.
4. Retry with an explicit Windows PowerShell executable path.
5. Retry in a subsequent conversation turn.

## Actual result
All of these attempts fail before the command runs:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"Failed to create unified exec process: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors\")" }
```

The same failure occurred for both a minimal read-only command and a repository inspection command. MCP tool calls still execute, so the observed failure is specific to local command execution rather than all tools.

## Expected result
Read-only PowerShell commands should execute in the configured workspace, or the application should return actionable diagnostics identifying which setup refresh step failed and how to recover.

## Impact
The agent cannot carry out an authorized code-review fix, inspect ownership/worktrees, or run validation.

## Additional observation
Separately, GitHub connector PR-read calls for the private target repository returned HTTP 404, while public repository search and the connected-user profile call succeeded. The cause of those 404s is unverified, and there is no evidence that they share a root cause with the local execution failure.

No restart recovery has been tested. No credentials, private source code, or private repository identifiers are included in this report.

Launch Windows daemon children in a dedicated working directory

## Why

Windows processes hold their working directory open for their lifetime, and sandbox setup may broaden its ACL. Managed children should avoid pinning the launching project's directory or changing permissions on the private daemon state directory.

## What changed

Create a `workdir` subdirectory alongside the PID files and use it as the working directory for both the managed app-server and updater on Windows.

## Testing

Add a Windows regression test covering both managed children. It verifies that relative files land in `workdir`, the state directory still passes private-directory validation, and stopping each child removes its PID file.

Capture host-supplied extension data for each turn

## What changed

Add `turn_extension_init` to thread startup and settings, and expose `WithTurnExtensionData` for turn input, recovery, and settings requests. Accept or reject data updates together with the request that supplies them.

Each new turn captures the configured data, including automatically started turns. Accepted steering updates the data for future turns while preserving the running turn's capture. Plain requests preserve the configured data; an empty initializer clears it. The data is not persisted and must be supplied again on cold resume.

Expose `current_turn_extension_data` to retrieve typed data only when the requested turn is still running and has not been cancelled.

Add an integration test covering initial capture, accepted and rejected steering, inheritance by an automatic turn, clearing future data without changing the active capture, and rejection of lookups for an earlier turn.

items.title: Preserve daemon diagnostics and include updater logs in reports
items.body:
Preserve daemon diagnostics and include updater logs in reports

## Why

Detached launches truncate stderr logs, losing details from previous failures. Updater handoffs can also leave existing writers with stale offsets after truncation.

## What changed

- Record daemon lifecycle and update stages with timings, outcomes, and typed OS errors, omitting error messages and context.
- Preserve the last 256 KiB of nonempty stderr logs before truncation and use append handles to prevent gaps during handoff. Preservation failures do not block launch.
- Attach current and previous updater log tails when log inclusion is enabled for a report, with a 512 KiB total limit and legacy filename fallback. Skip missing, empty, and nonregular files.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for diagnostic error redaction, bounded log preservation, append behavior during handoff, attachment selection, and updater logs in captured report uploads.

**What happens**
1. The local rule `codex_sandbox_offline_block_outbound` (Outbound, Block, scoped to the `CodexSandboxOffline`
   user SID) exists but is `Enabled=False` in both PersistentStore and ActiveStore. Cause of the disablement unknown.
2. A `codex exec` worker with `sandbox_mode=workspace-write`, `windows.sandbox="elevated"` and
   `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=false` runs a shell tool that connects to a listener on 127.0.0.1:
   prints `CONNECTED`, listener records the connection.
3. `windowsSandbox/setupStart {"mode":"elevated"}` returns `started:true`, then
   `windowsSandbox/setupCompleted {"mode":"elevated","success":true,"error":null}` after ~2.4 s, no UAC prompt.
   `.codex/.sandbox/sandbox.<date>.log` shows `read-acl-only mode: applying read ACLs` ... `setup binary completed`.
   `setup_marker.json` (version 5) is not rewritten. The firewall rule is still disabled; the probe still connects.

**Expected:** elevated setup verifies that the offline block rule exists, is enabled and is scoped to the offline
user, and repairs it (or reports `success:false` / a `HelperFirewall*` error) - also when the marker is current.
Alternatively: a documented way to force full provisioning (`WindowsSandboxSetupStartParams` only has `mode` and
`cwd`).

**Impact:** `setupCompleted success:true` cannot be used as evidence of network isolation; with the rule disabled,
`network_access=false` is not enforced for the elevated Windows sandbox.

**Further measured after forcing full provisioning** (renamed `setup_marker.json`, elevated setupStart with UAC):
the rule is recreated/enabled (Enabled=True, both stores), and the worker is now blocked to 1.1.1.1:443
(`PermissionError`). Loopback still connects: the rule's RemoteAddress is
`0.0.0.0-126.255.255.255,128.0.0.0-255.255.255.255,::,::2-ffff:...` - 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 are excluded.
The full provisioning also created `codex_sandbox_offline_block_loopback_tcp` / `_udp` (Outbound, Block,
RemoteAddress `127.0.0.0/255.0.0.0,::/127`, LocalUser = the CodexSandboxOffline SID, Enabled=True in both stores),
yet a direct TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 from the worker still succeeds (listener records the accept).
`codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/sandbox_smoketests.py` test 17b "WS: direct loopback blocked" expects this to fail in
workspace-write. Our reproduction uses `codex exec` with the flags above (not the smoke-test harness itself).
Is there an additional mechanism (e.g. AppContainer / WFP filter) that should enforce this, and how can we verify it?

items.body:
Allow microphone channel selection for voice conversations

## Why

Mixing every input on a multichannel audio device can include playback channels in microphone capture. Selecting only microphone inputs keeps those playback channels out of the captured audio.

## What changed

- Add `audio.microphone_channel` with one-based channel numbers, accepting a single value or an array such as `[1, 2]`. Leaving it unset preserves mixing of all inputs.
- Add an input-channel picker for the selected microphone when it has at least three channels. Require a nonempty selection and save it locally for the next voice conversation.
- Average only the selected channels, deduplicate selections, and reject empty or unavailable selections without falling back to other inputs.
- Clear saved channel selections when saving an input device and report configuration overrides that prevent the reset from taking effect.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for excluding playback channels, sample conversion, subset mixing, invalid selections, configuration loading, local persistence and overrides, and picker selection and cancellation. Update UI snapshots and verify channel selections are passed to the voice helper.

items.body:
### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

`openai.chatgpt 26.928.31416` (linux-x64)

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected in this report.

### Which IDE are you using?

VS Code.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

The VS Code internal fetch bridge serializes an undefined handler result using `JSON.stringify(o)`. This produces undefined rather than JSON text. The webview success handler subsequently calls `JSON.parse(e.bodyJsonString)` and rejects an otherwise successful request.

This is observed when releasing a queued follow-up send lock. Sanitized logs from October 1, 2026 (local time, UTC+8):

```text
10:35:28.203 [warning] Failed to release queued message send lock
conversationId=<redacted>
errorMessage="\"undefined\" is not valid JSON"
errorName=SyntaxError
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at e.onFetchResponse (.../webview/assets/app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js:3:1518)

10:45:29.373 [warning] Failed to release queued message send lock
conversationId=<same-thread-redacted>
errorMessage="\"undefined\" is not valid JSON"
errorName=SyntaxError
```

The user also observed a message being processed twice without intentionally sending it twice. In the local rollout, the same user text appears as two distinct user response items at:
- 2026-10-01T02:35:28.156Z
- 2026-10-01T02:45:29.271Z

These are separate message occurrences, not the normal response_item/event_msg pair for a single message.

**The parsing defect is confirmed; its causal relationship to the duplicate submission is not established.** The lock release handler performs its side effect before returning undefined, so the warning alone does not prove that the actual lock was not released.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The exact UI sequence for the duplicate submission has not yet been reduced to a deterministic reproduction. The serialization failure can be reproduced independently:

```js
const assert = require("node:assert/strict");

const handlerResult = undefined; // e.g. queued-follow-up-send-lock-release
const response = {
  responseType: "success",
  status: 200,
  bodyJsonString: JSON.stringify(handlerResult),
};

// The success response has no "body" property:
assert.throws(() => JSON.parse(response.bodyJsonString), SyntaxError);
```

Inspection of the installed bundle found:
- `queued-follow-up-send-lock-release` calls `this.queuedFollowUpSendLocks.release(...)` without returning a value.
- The internal VS Code fetch bridge returns `bodyJsonString: JSON.stringify(o)`.
- The webview success handler uses `"body" in e ? e.body : JSON.parse(e.bodyJsonString)`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Successful internal requests with no return value should resolve without a JSON parsing error. Queued messages should be processed once, with successful submissions removed from the queue.

### Additional information

A local workaround changed only the internal bridge serialization expression:

```diff
- bodyJsonString: JSON.stringify(o)
+ bodyJsonString: JSON.stringify(o ?? null)
```

Validation:
- Reproduced the original undefined parsing failure.
- Checked round trips for undefined, null, an object, false, 0, an empty string, an empty array, and an acquired=false object (8 cases).
- `node --check` passed for the modified bundle.
- Verified the installed file differs from its backup only by the intended expression.

This is a local installed-bundle workaround, not an upstream source patch. End-to-end verification after reloading VS Code, including whether duplicate messages stop, is still pending.

Potential investigation lead, not a confirmed cause: the installed send-lock implementation retains sent-message IDs for `6e5` milliseconds (10 minutes), close to the observed 601-second gap. This does not establish that both submissions used the same client message ID.

Logs and code were inspected with assistance from Codex. Local paths and conversation identifiers are redacted.

### What issue are you seeing?

In the Codex TUI, a local Markdown link with an explicit label does not keep that label as the visible link text.

For example, assume the current working directory is:

```text
/tmp/codex-link-repro
```

and the assistant outputs:

```markdown
[analysis.md](/tmp/codex-link-repro/analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group/analysis.md)
```

I would expect the rendered transcript to display:

```text
analysis.md
```

with `analysis.md` acting as the clickable file reference.

Instead, Codex renders:

```text
analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group/analysis.md
```

The original Markdown label:

```text
analysis.md
```

is discarded and replaced by a cwd-relative version of the destination path.

Normal Markdown separates the visible text from the destination:

```text
[label](destination)
```

For local file links, Codex currently changes this relationship by replacing a path-like label with the normalized local target.

This also makes responses significantly noisier when the assistant intentionally uses short file names as labels.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a small test workspace:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/codex-link-repro/analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group
printf '# test\n' > /tmp/codex-link-repro/analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group/analysis.md
cd /tmp/codex-link-repro
```

2. Start Codex CLI from:

```text
/tmp/codex-link-repro
```

3. Ask the assistant to output exactly this Markdown link:

```markdown
[analysis.md](/tmp/codex-link-repro/analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group/analysis.md)
```

4. Observe the rendered assistant transcript.

Actual visible text:

```text
analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group/analysis.md
```

Expected visible text:

```text
analysis.md
```

The explicit Markdown label is not preserved.

### What is the expected behavior?

The Markdown label should remain the visible text:

```text
analysis.md
```

If the destination resolves to a valid file inside the current workspace and passes Codex's local-file safety checks, the visible label should be a clickable file reference whose target is the resolved local file.

Conceptually:

```text
[analysis.md](/workspace/analysis/021/.../analysis.md)
     │                         │
     │ visible label           │ file destination
     ▼                         ▼
 analysis.md  ───────────►  local file
   clickable
```

The destination path does not need to replace the Markdown label in the rendered transcript.

If Codex cannot safely validate the destination as a local workspace file, it can keep a safe non-clickable fallback without creating a file hyperlink.

### Additional information

I checked the current TUI implementation, and this appears to come from the local-link rendering policy, not from the Markdown parser itself.

Relevant files:

```text
codex-rs/tui/src/markdown_render/local_links.rs
codex-rs/tui/src/markdown_render.rs
codex-rs/tui/src/terminal_hyperlinks.rs
codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/spoken_artifacts.rs
```

In `local_links.rs`, `display_local_link_path()` shortens an absolute local path relative to the current working directory.

There is also an explicit label policy in `should_render_local_link_label()`:

```rust
/// Decide whether a local-file link label adds meaning beyond its canonical target.
///
/// Matching path-like labels collapse to the target; prose labels remain visible.
```

For a link such as:

```markdown
[analysis.md](/tmp/codex-link-repro/analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group/analysis.md)
```

`analysis.md` is considered a path-like suffix of the destination, so the label is collapsed and the normalized target is rendered instead.

This appears to explain the exact output:

```text
analysis/021_all_experiments_best_per_group/analysis.md
```

Codex already has semantic terminal hyperlink support and a separate trusted local-file mechanism through:

```text
TrustedWorkspaceFile
TerminalHyperlink::trusted_workspace_file()
```

A possible implementation direction would be:

1. Preserve the Markdown label as the visible span.
2. Resolve the local destination.
3. If it resolves to a valid file inside the session workspace and passes the existing local-file validation, attach a trusted OSC 8 file hyperlink to the label.
4. If validation fails, keep a safe fallback without promoting an arbitrary local path to a clickable `file://` URI.

This would keep the existing safety checks while restoring the expected Markdown behavior:

```markdown
[analysis.md](local-file-target)
```

Rendered as:

```text
analysis.md
```

with the validated local file as the hyperlink target.

Related issues:

- #17922 — Feature request: native OSC 8 clickable terminal links in interactive TUI
- #25934 — TUI markdown hyperlinks are not clickable in OSC 8-capable terminals

#17922 was closed after semantic OSC 8 hyperlinks were added.

This issue is more specific: local Markdown links with path-like labels currently replace the explicit Markdown label with the normalized local target, even though the link already contains a display label.

A read-only check of the available Codex browser TOML configuration did not find an archive.org allow or deny entry. - Google Chrome browser integration, not the built-in browser

items.body: ### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? 0.159.2 ### What subscription do you have? $200/month pro ### What platform is your computer? MacOS Tahoe 26.6 ### What issue are you seeing? # Codex CLI 0.159.2 writes false project evidence after forcing zsh and breaking PATH ## Bug description After Codex prompted me to upgrade to `codex-cli 0.159.2`, it began treating its own shell and PATH failures as evidence about the projects under test. It wrote incorrect conclusions into durable design documents and test reports, including statements such as `X is blocked because of access restrictions` and `Y is unproven due to tool failures`. It wrote false test results. These were not product failures, test failures or access failures. Codex had invoked the wrong shell or resolved macOS Bash 3.2 after changing the effective PATH. It then recorded the resulting command failure as though it described the system under test. This caused actual damage to project records: - false blockers were added to design documents; - tests were recorded as unproven for reasons unrelated to the product; - shell failures became incorrect service-access findings; - later work inherited those false conclusions as established evidence. Most of my shell scripts, development commands and custom Codex skills require Bash 5. They worked before this version bump. ## Underlying shell regression Codex repeatedly invokes `/bin/zsh` despite all of the following: - my macOS account login shell is `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`, configured through `chsh`; - Codex is launched through a wrapper running Homebrew Bash 5; - the wrapper exports `SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`; - the wrapper verifies the inherited `PATH` before starting Codex; - the wrapper uses `exec` to replace itself with Codex while preserving that validated environment; - `shell_environment_policy.inherit = "all"` is set in `config.toml`. The wrapper confirms the environment in which Codex starts: ```text Wrapper for /opt/homebrew/bin/bash Executing with bash 5.3.9(1)-release: codex ``` Codex nevertheless attempts to execute tool commands through zsh. It also changes or reconstructs `PATH` in a way that can place macOS system paths ahead of my configured tool paths. When it eventually tries Bash, this resolves `/bin/bash`, the obsolete Bash 3.2 shipped with macOS, instead of `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`. ## Workaround and remaining failure To stop Codex from silently converting shell failures into project evidence, I took the nuclear option and disabled zsh through `~/.zshenv`. Every unwanted zsh invocation now fails immediately and identifies the environment error explicitly: ```sh # /etc/zshenv echo "⛔️ zsh is banned on this system." >&2 echo "For POSIX shell scripts on Darwin use /opt/homebrew/bin/bash" >&2 echo "DO NOT PREPEND THE PATH WITH YOUR OWN STUFF OR IT WILL BREAK THINGS." >&2 echo "If in doubt, source ~/.envrc to obtain the correct PATH" >&2 exit 1 ``` Every command now follows the same cycle: 1. Codex invokes zsh. 2. `.zshenv` rejects the invocation. 3. Codex reads the error and retries with `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`. 4. The command succeeds. 5. On the next tool call, Codex invokes zsh again. 6. Return to step 1. This prevents the original evidence corruption: Codex sees an explicit shell error and retries under `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash` instead of treating the failure as a product result. It does not make Codex usable. On every tool call, Codex invokes zsh, reads the failure, reasons its way back to Bash 5, runs the command, and then starts with zsh again on the next call. Work that previously took minutes now runs for hours. Simple questions become long-running sessions, while substantive development work never reaches its intended result. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? ## Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS, install Bash 5 through Homebrew at `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`. 2. Set `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash` as the account login shell with `chsh`. 3. Launch Codex through Bash 5 from an environment whose `PATH` resolves `bash` to the Homebrew installation. 4. Before launching Codex: - verify that Bash is version 5 or later; - verify the expected first entry in `PATH`; - export `SHELL=/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`. 5. Use `exec` to start Codex from that Bash process, preserving the validated environment. 6. Configure Codex with: ```toml allow_login_shell = false [shell_environment_policy] inherit = "all" ``` 7. Start Codex and ask it to run a basic command such as: ```sh echo "$SHELL" ``` ### What is the expected behavior? ## Expected behaviour Codex should preserve the inherited environment and execute commands using the shell supplied through `SHELL`, or provide a first-class configuration setting for the command shell. At minimum, it should not: - assume that zsh is the user's shell merely because the operating system is macOS; - invoke `/bin/zsh` when both the login shell and `SHELL` explicitly name Homebrew Bash; - reconstruct or prepend `PATH` so that `/bin/bash` takes precedence over `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`; - retry a shell that has already failed on every subsequent tool call. `allow_login_shell = false` should control login-shell behaviour. It should not cause Codex to ignore the configured shell executable. ## Regression This workflow operated correctly before the upgrade to `0.159.2`. The failure began immediately after Codex prompted me to install that version. ## Environment - Codex CLI: `0.159.2` - Operating system: macOS - Login shell: `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash` - Intended command shell: `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash` - Bash version: `5.3.9(1)-release` - Codex sandbox mode: `danger-full-access` - Approval policy: `never` - Environment policy: `inherit = "all"` The complete `config.toml` parses successfully, and Codex reads other settings from it. ## Possibly related issues - #10920: Codex wraps commands in `/bin/zsh -lc` - #3916: Codex does not respect the user's configured shell - #20220: zsh shell snapshots omit `PATH`, breaking Homebrew tools The reported behaviour overlaps with those issues, but this case affects the terminal-launched CLI even though it inherits a validated PATH and an explicit `SHELL` value. ### Additional information _No response_

**Environment:** ChatGPT desktop `26.928.31416` (build `12553`), macOS
**Subscription:** ChatGPT Pro

Opening a Dot-created task in desktop fails with:

```text
Failed to resume chat
Codex app-server is not available
```

The same task opens successfully in ChatGPT web.

**Reproduction**

1. Use a network where direct access to `codex-cloud-backend.chatgpt.com` times out but an approved proxy works.
2. Configure system/app proxy settings, including `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`.
3. Open a Dot-created task in desktop.

Logs repeatedly show `hostKind=durable`, `failureReason=open_timeout`, and WebSocket close code `1006`.

**Findings**

Installed-code inspection suggests the bundled WebSocket library supplies a custom `createConnection` without a proxy agent, bypassing Node’s environment-aware default agent. A standalone reproduction timed out with that configuration and received a response after adding an explicit proxy-aware agent.

The proxy independently passed full WSS handshake and message-echo tests over both HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5. An authenticated desktop fix has not yet been tested.

**Space Pages**

The same Page opens on the web, but desktop ends with “Could not connect to ChatGPT”. The desktop `pagesRealtime` path uses the same WebSocket library without an explicit proxy agent. The same bypass is suspected; the failing request is not yet confirmed. Please test Space Pages too—a Dot-only fix may leave this broken.

**Expected behavior / possible fixes**

- Honor configured proxies for the durable WebSocket transport.
- Consider also honoring `CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_URL` on this path. It currently bypasses that override; supporting it could enable an application-scoped relay workaround.

This matters in FDE/client environments requiring approved proxy access without additional system-wide traffic interception.

Do not use tools or modify files."}]}` 6. observe notifications until terminal state ## Expected - agent message deltas and final text - `turn/completed` with `turn.status = "completed"` ## Actual (4/4 product-path attempts on 2026-10-01) - `thread/start` and `turn/start` are accepted (valid ids returned) - mid-turn error notifications: - `message: "workspace routing discovery failed"` - `codexErrorInfo: "other"`, `additionalDetails: null`, `misalignment: null` - terminal `willRetry: false` - in one run the server first emitted 9 × `willRetry: true` notifications, then the same terminal error - no agent message, no file or tool side effects; the app-server exits cleanly on stdin EOF (exit code 0) - failure time: ~13-15s after `turn/start`, regardless of workspace path shape ## Controls 1. **Same binary, same contract, earlier date (2026-09-30):** an app-server turn over the identical protocol sequence (including `initialized`) completed successfully in ~6.6s with `status=completed`. The client contract therefore has a success precedent on 0.159.2. 2. **Different entry, same day as failures:** native `codex exec` with the same prompt and login succeeded (`PROBE_OK`). This only proves the exec entry works — it does **not** prove app-server routing health. 3. **Path shape ruled out:** a shallow stable path and a deep pytest-shaped path fail with the byte-identical error; the failing client's outbound `thread/start.cwd` was verified character-exact against the existing directory. 4. **`initialized` ruled out as sufficient cause:** after the client fixed its handshake to send `initialized` (per official docs), the turn still failed with the identical routing error (after 9 retries). 5. **Clean lifecycle:** every failing app-server instance exits with code 0 on stdin EOF; no orphan processes. ## Requests to upstream 1. What preconditions does `"workspace routing discovery failed"` (`codexErrorInfo=other`) indicate, and which side is expected to satisfy them? 2. Is default provider + Codex CLI login state a supported combination for app-server `turn/start`? 3. Are there undocumented workspace registration / routing / trust requirements for app-server turns (beyond `thread/start.cwd` pointing at an existing directory)? 4. items.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?

26.924.22138 (macOS app bundle version; About dialog not checked).

## What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT PRO ($200)

## What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm` (`uname -mprs`).

## What issue are you seeing?

The OpenAI-curated remote tldraw connector can return a successful `tldraw_exec` result from an older editor state for a board that is also open on tldraw.com. Edits made through that connector state appeared in its side-panel view but were not visible on the same board in Chrome. The agent treated the successful tool result as a saved edit and incorrectly told the user the board had been updated.

For the affected board, `tldraw_list_open_boards` listed **three editable views with the same board ID**, including one with a default name and two with the board title. The `tldraw_exec` API accepts only `boardId`, not `viewId`. A read-only `exec` returned an earlier version of a text shape. The same shape in the tldraw.com board, viewed in Chrome after reload, contained later text. Calling `tldraw_open_board` again and then `exec` still returned the earlier text. The affected board contains private organizational material, so its URL and text are omitted from this public issue; I can provide details privately.

This is **not** a claim that all connector writes fail. On a fresh, nonsensitive test board, `tldraw_exec` created a text shape and Chrome showed it after load. I then changed the text in Chrome; a subsequent connector `exec` read the new text. That control board is https://www.tldraw.com/f/IBgF38IUZHtEv2yeYlIpl.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?

The affected long-lived board had multiple open connector views. I cannot yet reproduce the divergence from a fresh board, but this is the observed sequence:

1. Open an existing tldraw.com board through the Codex tldraw plugin in more than one side-panel view. `tldraw_list_open_boards` can show multiple editable `viewId` entries for one `boardId`.
2. Edit a text shape through `tldraw_exec({boardId, code})`. The tool returns a successful result and updated shape count/content.
3. Open or reload the same board URL in Chrome. The edited text is absent there.
4. Edit that shape in Chrome, then read it through `tldraw_exec`. The connector can still return the earlier text, even after `tldraw_open_board({action:"open", boardId})`.

I used the tldraw plugin identified in Codex as `app-6ab242dbeb5c8191ba5277534ef0c570@openai-curated-remote` on 2026-10-01. No error was returned for the stale reads or earlier edits. The connector's exact version is not exposed to me.

## What is the expected behavior?

An `exec` call for a `boardId` should operate on the latest shared board state and its successful edits should be visible at the same tldraw.com URL after reload. If a selected editor view is stale, disconnected, or unable to persist, the tool should report that instead of presenting local success as a committed board edit. If multiple views are open, the target view should be explicit or selected deterministically.

## Additional information

The fresh-board control suggests this may depend on multiple open views, stale editor state, or a persistence race. That is an investigation lead, not a confirmed root cause. A useful diagnostic would be the `viewId` selected by each `exec` call and an acknowledgement that the edit reached the shared tldraw document.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

ChatGPT/Codex desktop app with dots, across macOS and Windows.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please allow a single dot to keep more than one personal computer authorized and available at the same time, select the execution device for each task, and run independent tasks on different devices in parallel.

#### Use case and current behavior

I use both a Mac and a Windows PC. Some files and apps are available on only one of them, so I would like the same dot to work on the appropriate computer without repeated reconnecting or switching authorization.

In my current setup, granting the dot access to the second personal computer removes its task authorization on the first. Both computers can remain online, but only one is available for the dot's local tasks.

The [official computer-access documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/computers-and-apps#connect-your-computer) says that only one personal computer can be connected at a time. This is a request to expand that documented capability.

#### Requested behavior

- Keep multiple personal computers authorized independently for the same dot
- Let me explicitly choose a device per task, or ask the dot to use a specific authorized device
- Allow independent tasks to run on different authorized devices at the same time
- Show each device's connection and authorization status, and clearly label where each task is running
- Let me revoke one device without removing access to the others
- Preserve existing permission checks and approvals on each device

### Additional information

This request concerns the personal-computer connection in the dots desktop experience. It does not assume that registered Remotes, headless servers, or other execution environments have the same limitation.

I searched existing issues. #49503 concerns per-device task visibility, and #49487 concerns revoking or replacing an offline device; neither appears to cover simultaneous personal-computer authorization and execution.

Is a supported multi-personal-computer workflow already available, or is this capability planned? If dots feature requests belong in another official tracker, please point me to the appropriate place.

This is a text-only feature request; no private device identifiers, account diagnostics, screenshots, or logs are included.

- the environment appeared to have been reset or reprovisioned

items.body:
## Summary

A Dot-connected Windows task can run shell commands but fail to start the native `codex_app` MCP server because its child environment lacks `SystemRoot`. After separating the MSIX working-directory problem, a controlled native-executor A/B isolated the remaining failure to the environment: the original launcher exits before MCP initialization; restoring only launcher-local `SystemRoot` makes initialization and the 55-tool catalog succeed.

The public remote-MCP implementation constructs its explicit environment allowlist using the controller build's OS-specific defaults. That is unsafe when a Unix controller launches a Windows MCP child. This is a narrower RCA than the general missing-tool reports.

## Environment

- Windows 11 x64, Microsoft Store/MSIX Desktop.
- Original successful repair: Desktop 26.928.21956, build 12404; package 26.928.2636.0.
- Post-update reproduction and repair: Desktop 26.928.31416, build 12553; package 26.928.3736.0.
- Bundled native Windows and active WSL agents: 0.159.2.
- Ordinary Desktop project execution uses WSL; the connected-computer executor used by the affected Dot worker is native Windows. These are different execution paths.
- The worker is cloud-coordinated. We do not have its hosted controller's deployed binary/build metadata.

## Evidence and causal isolation

1. A separate MSIX export/cwd defect first prevented the unpackaged executor from reaching the app-tools export. That is covered by #49562. A narrowly scoped directory bridge restored path visibility.
2. With a valid configured cwd, a private, owned instance of the official native `exec-server` reproduced the product's raw MCP `process/start` path, not the ordinary restricted shell sandbox.
3. Its child environment used the Unix core allowlist plus exactly the generated MCP manifest's declared remote variables and explicit values. `SystemRoot` was absent. The manifest did not declare it.
4. The bundled Node aborted before MCP initialization. Earlier controlled tests captured `Assertion failed: ncrypto::CSPRNG(nullptr, 0)`. Adding only `SYSTEMROOT` to the forwarded environment prevented that abort.
5. A temporary marker in the actual delegated worker's launcher independently recorded SystemRoot absent before recovery and present afterward. That worker then reached server-ready, received 55 app-control tools on the following turn, and successfully read and messaged an existing local Desktop chat. The marker was removed; only the minimal guard remained.
6. Updating Desktop regenerated the export and removed that guard. The current-build controlled test again failed before initialize. Restoring the same one-line guard fixed the identical test without changing the manifest, cwd, runtime selection, permissions, or global environment.

Current-build result, October 1 UTC:

| Test | Original exported launcher | Restored local guard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official owned executor initialize | PASS | PASS |
| MCP child process/start | PASS | PASS |
| SystemRoot explicitly forwarded by test | No | No |
| MCP initialize | Child stdout closed before reply | PASS |
| Read-only tools/list | Not reached | PASS, 55 tools |
| Owned child/executor cleanup | Confirmed stopped | Confirmed stopped |

The after-test catalog includes `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, and `send_message_to_thread`. The current post-update test did not invoke these tools or assume every previously failed chat client had refreshed.

## Source pointer

Verified at public main commit `cda82a2c6853b484e0ba56d38f13902adfb2a6a1`:

- [ExecutorStdioServerLauncher::remote_env_policy](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/cda82a2c6853b484e0ba56d38f13902adfb2a6a1/codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/stdio_server_launcher.rs#L682) uses `crate::utils::DEFAULT_ENV_VARS` to build `include_only` whenever explicit remote variables exist.
- [DEFAULT_ENV_VARS](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/cda82a2c6853b484e0ba56d38f13902adfb2a6a1/codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/utils.rs#L162) is selected by `#[cfg(unix)]` / `#[cfg(windows)]`, meaning the controller's compilation target. The Unix set omits SystemRoot.
- The generated native app-tools manifest has nonempty `env_vars`, but neither its forwarded list nor its explicit environment supplies SystemRoot.

This source explains the reproduced cross-platform allowlist behavior. We are not claiming access to, or exact version identity with, the hosted controller deployment.

## Temporary workaround and update behavior

On this host, after verifying the export resolves to the correct product-owned directory and matches the installed vendor launcher/server, this line immediately after `setlocal` restores the value only when absent:

```bat
if not defined SystemRoot for %%I in ("%__APPDIR__%..") do set "SystemRoot=%%~fI"
```

It derives the Windows directory from the running cmd.exe location; it does not copy controller environment values, change global environment, broaden inheritance, edit the signed package, or change pipe ACLs.

This is not an update-proof fix: Desktop's export reconciliation legitimately replaces the generated launcher, so the underlying startup bug returns. Please fix the environment construction/export rather than preserve user patches. A successful `node --version` alone is not a sufficient control for Node executing the actual MCP server.

## Requested fix and regression coverage

- Select essential remote-process environment variables using the executor OS, not the controller compilation target; preserve explicitly requested variables without inheriting the entire environment.
- Add a Unix-controller to Windows-executor test with nonempty remote `env_vars`; verify target-side SystemRoot reaches the child.
- Test actual bundled Node JavaScript/MCP initialization and tools/list, not only binary existence or version output.
- Preserve useful sanitized process-exit/stderr information. The affected Desktop log otherwise reports only `MCP server failed to start.`
- Verify the path/environment behavior survives export regeneration and Desktop updates.

## Related but separate

- #49562: MSIX native export working directory; fixing this alone did not solve our environment failure.
- #49488: durable MCP startup failures and a separate follow-up path error.
- #49458: missing Computer Use in Dot-created Windows tasks. Restoring app controls did **not** restore direct Chrome/CUA in our worker; that remains separate.

Managed daemons and updaters can outlive their launching directory. Restarts and updater replacement need to keep working after that directory is removed.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT Desktop 26.928.2636.0 (Microsoft Store), package OpenAI.Codex_26.928.2636.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0 (previous version tested: 26.917.9434.0 — same behavior)

### What subscription do you have?

Unknown

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Home (Chinese), 24H2, build 26100, x64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Description
On ChatGPT Desktop 26.928.2636.0 (Windows, Microsoft Store), `codex.exe` is launched normally by `ChatGPT.exe` and attempts to connect to `127.0.0.1:57321`, but the application never starts any Gateway process and never attempts to bind/listen on port 57321. The UI shows "Reconnecting... waiting for network" forever. A clean reinstall produces the same behavior.

## Actual
- `codex.exe` (child of `ChatGPT.exe`) runs `app-server` and retries `http://127.0.0.1:57321/v1/responses` forever (`SYN_SENT`, never `ESTABLISHED`).
- No process ever binds/listens on 57321 during the entire app lifecycle (verified from cold start through message send).
- No separate gateway subprocess exists — process tree is only `ChatGPT.exe` (Electron) + `codex.exe`.
- Searching the bundled `app.asar`: all 98 `gateway` matches are `gatewayOAuth` (login flow); no server-side `listen` on 57321 found.

## Summary
The app knows the gateway should be on 57321 (it writes the config), spawns `codex.exe` correctly, but the gateway initialization path itself never executes — not a startup failure, but a startup that never happens.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install ChatGPT from Microsoft Store, log in.
2. Open the app, send any message.
3. UI shows "Reconnecting... waiting for network" indefinitely.
4. Run `netstat -ano | findstr 57321` — a `codex.exe` process shows `SYN_SENT` to `127.0.0.1:57321`, but there is no `LISTEN` on 57321.

### What is the expected behavior?

The app should start a local gateway listening on 127.0.0.1:57321, since it writes `~/.codex/config.toml` with:
```toml
model_provider = "custom"
[model_providers.custom]
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:57321/v1"
```

### Additional information

## Ruled out
- Port conflict: 57321 binds fine manually (tested with a temporary listener).
- Crash: no Crashpad dump; no error in Windows Event Viewer (Application log, 3h window).
- Corrupt install: full `Remove-AppxPackage` + Store reinstall to a newer version — same result.
- User state: individually isolated/renamed `LocalCache`, `runtimes`, `chrome-native-hosts-v2.json`, `Settings/settings.dat` — no change.
- Proxy: an earlier 502 was caused by a third-party system proxy intercepting loopback; fixed via `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost,::1` + reboot. The current issue persists with the proxy bypassed.

items.title: Add coordinated shutdown for local agent trees
items.body:
Add coordinated shutdown for local agent trees

## What changed

Expose `ThreadManager::request_agent_tree_shutdown` and an `AgentTreeShutdown::wait` handle. Requests reject new starts in the shared runtime, cancel pending startup, and signal every session in that tree, including delegates outside the thread registry. Waiting covers admitted operations and session teardown, and reports cleanup or persistence writer failures. Other root trees remain unaffected; registry removal and persistence handoff remain caller responsibilities.

Retain tree membership through startup, cancelled spawn cleanup, residency eviction, and completion watchers. Release persistence resources before returning startup failures, and stop completion watchers during tree shutdown without reporting shutdown as a child result.

## Testing

Add coverage for tree isolation, children removed from the registry, delegate teardown, cancellation during required MCP initialization, aborted teardown, persistence writer failures, and successful retry after a failed resume releases its writer.

Move shadow skill ranking off the turn preparation path

## Why

Shadow skill selection runs synchronously during turn input construction, making turn preparation wait for experimental rankings.

## What changed

Run ranking on background blocking workers with a process-wide limit of two concurrent rankings. Wait for capacity in the background and hold each slot until its blocking worker finishes, even if the async evaluation is cancelled.

Freeze catalog, query, and relevance history at turn start. Record eligible invocations immediately for future turns, then score queued observations against the frozen rankings once they are ready, including observations queued before the turn state is dropped.

## Testing
